title: Place instructions at the narrowest stable scope
evidenceNote: Cited PDF pages support the named mechanism. Repository scenarios, exercises, recovery demonstrations, and grading criteria are instructor-authored professional applications.
plainLanguage: Instruction hierarchy lets global preferences, repository rules, and directory-specific conventions coexist. A rule should live at the narrowest scope where it is always true. Root rules apply broadly; nested files specialize work in a package or directory. Broad placement wastes context and can make a correct rule wrong elsewhere.
mentalModel: Treat place instructions at the narrowest stable scope as a repository protocol: Show load scopes and place rules at the narrowest stable level. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: Locality reduces irrelevant context, conditional ambiguity, and ownership drift while preserving shared constraints.
mechanism: Pages 8–10 illustrate hierarchical loading. In a monorepo, root instructions define shared commands and boundaries; `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` may define UI tests; `services/payments/CLAUDE.md` may define ledger invariants. Narrow files reduce conditional prose and allow ownership near the code. Conflicts require a documented precedence model and testing in the actual working directory.
useWhen: Use it for The root requires pnpm and global checks. The web package requires accessibility tests and component conventions. The payments service forbids destructive migration edits. Placing all three at root would send irrelevant UI detail into backend work and risk applying migration rules to unrelated packages.

avoidWhen: Avoid this mechanism when a single deterministic command solves the task with lower coordination cost.

title: Reveal detailed instructions only when needed
evidenceNote: Cited PDF pages support the named mechanism. Repository scenarios, exercises, recovery demonstrations, and grading criteria are instructor-authored professional applications.
plainLanguage: Progressive disclosure keeps automatically loaded instructions short and links to detailed guidance that is opened only for a relevant task. mentalModel: Treat reveal detailed instructions only when needed as a repository protocol: Keep the root concise; link conditional detail and indexes instead of preloading everything. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: More context can bury the applicable rule. Selective loading improves signal without abandoning traceable detail.
mechanism: Pages 15–21 argue that less automatic context can improve instruction adherence. A useful link states when to read the target, not merely its filename. The agent loads database migration guidance when a migration is involved, not during a CSS change. Conditional retrieval must remain reliable: critical safety rules cannot be hidden behind a link the agent may never open and should be enforced mechanically.

title: Collision-free parallel work boundaries
evidenceNote: Cited PDF pages support the named mechanism. Repository scenarios, exercises, recovery demonstrations, and grading criteria are instructor-authored professional applications.
plainLanguage: Collision-free parallel work boundaries is the discipline of applying this source rule in a real engineering system: Keep persistent utilities and independent tasks in separate named tabs so context and processes remain visible and do not interfere. In Constellation monorepo, it controls a named decision rather than serving as a slogan.
mentalModel: Picture collision-free parallel work boundaries as the control point between plans/ownership-matrix.md and isolated worktrees and non-overlapping ownership, explicit handoffs, isolated branches, and an integration report. The source's decisive distinction is: Define ownership, shared contracts, branch/worktree, completion artifact, and integrator.
whyItMatters: Without this control, the technical lead can receive a plausible narrative while repository state remains wrong. The resulting cost—an unreproducible decision, unsafe transition, or ownerless regression—follows directly from this source observation: Keep persistent utilities and independent tasks in separate named tabs so context and processes remain visible and do not interfere.
mechanism: The mechanism operates on plans/ownership-matrix.md and isolated worktrees. First it exposes the relevant state; then it applies Define ownership, shared contracts, branch/worktree, completion artifact, and integrator. title: Decide when a Ralph loop fits
evidenceNote: Cited PDF pages support the named mechanism. Repository scenarios, exercises, recovery demonstrations, and grading criteria are instructor-authored professional applications.
plainLanguage: A Ralph loop repeatedly gives Claude a bounded unit of work, lets it inspect durable project state, and starts another iteration until an externally visible completion condition is reached. The important decision is not whether the loop sounds powerful; it is whether the work produces reliable evidence on every iteration. Ralph fits tasks such as implementing a list of independent stories, raising test coverage, or validating several technical approaches because files, tests, builds, and task flags expose progress. It is a poor fit for ambiguous taste, one-way production actions, unclear ownership, or work whose success can only be judged after deployment by a person.
mentalModel: Treat decide when a ralph loop fits as a repository protocol: Use for bounded, testable, file-observable iteration; avoid ambiguous taste, unsafe external effects, and weak verification. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: The weak request delegates the definition of done, retry policy, scope, and authority. The improved brief supplies observable state, independent verification, reversible execution, explicit budgets, and escalation exits—the conditions that make repetition safer than a long interactive session.
mechanism: Pages 7–10 frame Ralph around two recurring problems: long trajectories accumulate misleading context, and an agent may claim completion without satisfying the repository. Repeated fresh iterations reduce trajectory contamination, while durable files carry forward only selected state. This helps only when each iteration can read an explicit objective, choose a small unfinished item, change a reversible workspace, and run a verifier. A completion phrase is never sufficient evidence. The loop controller, repository state, tests, budgets, and approval boundaries form the actual control system.
useWhen: Use it for A TypeScript service has twelve migration stories. Each story has acceptance tests, all work occurs in a disposable worktree, and CI-equivalent commands run locally. This is a strong Ralph candidate. A request to ‘make the dashboard feel premium’ has no stable grader and is not. A request to rotate production secrets has irreversible external effects and must remain human-controlled.

Use it when Claude can stop when code looks complete and degrade as a long context fills. Ralph forces a completion signal tied to checks and lets each iteration inspect durable files from a cleaner context.
avoidWhen: Avoid this mechanism when a single deterministic command solves the task with lower coordination cost.
Do not promote autonomy until the submitted mastery rubric passes in a clean review.

title: Understand the Ralph stop-hook mechanism
evidenceNote: Cited PDF pages support the named mechanism. Repository scenarios, exercises, recovery demonstrations, and grading criteria are instructor-authored professional applications.
plainLanguage: Ralph is a control loop built around Claude Code's attempt to stop. When Claude reaches the end of an iteration, a stop hook examines durable state. If verified work remains, the hook prevents final termination and starts another iteration with the original objective plus current project state. If every task is genuinely verified—or a safety budget says execution must end—the controller allows the session to stop. The hook controls continuation; it does not prove correctness.
mentalModel: Treat understand the ralph stop-hook mechanism as a repository protocol: A completion promise is a control token, not proof; the hook recycles work until bounded conditions are met. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: A phrase is model output; completion is repository state plus evidence. The improved controller treats the phrase as a handshake after verification, not the verifier itself, and makes the reason for every continuation or exit inspectable.
mechanism: Pages 11–16 separate three ideas that are easily confused. The stop hook is the continuation mechanism. The repository, task file, and progress log are the state mechanism. The completion promise is a protocol token Claude emits only after its checks say the work is done. A robust controller independently checks task flags, command results, and budgets before trusting that token. This closes a common loophole: a model can sincerely say ‘done’ after checking only the last edit. External state must show that the whole acceptance contract is satisfied.
useWhen: Use it for A Python library must make all stories in prd.json pass `pytest`, `ruff check`, and `mypy`. The loop runs one story, records evidence, attempts to stop, and the controller checks whether any task remains unpassed. A failure or unfinished task triggers another bounded iteration; a permission request or exhausted budget exits to a human instead of recycling.

Use it when Ralph repeatedly sends a prompt to Claude rather than accepting the first perceived completion. Failure is expected; artifacts left in files become evidence for the next iteration. The basic historical form is a Bash while loop; the Anthropic plugin form uses a Stop hook.
avoidWhen: Avoid this mechanism when a single deterministic command solves the task with lower coordination cost.

title: Turn a PRD into atomic prd.json tasks
evidenceNote: Cited PDF pages support the named mechanism. Repository scenarios, exercises, recovery demonstrations, and grading criteria are instructor-authored professional applications.
plainLanguage: The product requirements document explains the outcome and constraints for humans. `prd.json` turns that intent into the small state machine the loop can execute. A task is atomic when one iteration can understand it, change a bounded area, and decide pass or fail using explicit acceptance criteria. Atomic does not mean one file or one function; it means one independently verifiable behavior.
mentalModel: Treat turn a prd into atomic prd.json tasks as a repository protocol: Each task needs acceptance criteria, dependencies, priority, and machine-checkable completion. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: Layer names hide multiple behaviors and produce late integration surprises. Behavior tasks expose dependencies, keep iterations attributable, and give the controller a reliable state transition. The reviewed PRD protects the loop from solving a locally coherent but globally incorrect problem.
mechanism: Pages 17–23 show a two-stage design. First generate and review the PRD so the product boundary is stable. Then derive prioritized tasks with IDs, descriptions, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and a pass flag. The loop selects a high-priority task whose dependencies have passed. It must not mark the flag from confidence or code appearance: the acceptance evidence determines the transition. Human PRD review prevents an autonomous loop from efficiently implementing the wrong product.
useWhen: Use it for Add passwordless email login to an existing web app. The reviewed PRD preserves password login, forbids storing raw tokens, requires expiration and one-time use, and excludes account merging. The executable tasks separate schema, token service, request endpoint, consume endpoint, UI, and end-to-end verification according to dependency order.

plainLanguage: A fresh Ralph iteration should not inherit the whole conversation, but it still needs to know what happened. `progress.txt` is the chronological execution journal: task attempted, files changed, commands run, results, and current blocker. `agents.md` is curated project knowledge: stable commands, architectural rules, verified gotchas, and patterns future iterations should follow. One answers ‘what happened recently?’; the other answers ‘what remains true about this project?’
mentalModel: Treat separate progress.txt from durable agents.md knowledge as a repository protocol: Separate chronological execution log from durable project patterns and gotchas. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: Maximum retention is not maximum usefulness. The two-file policy lets the operator reconstruct execution while protecting future decision context from transient noise. Promotion criteria create a deliberate memory boundary.
mechanism: Pages 23–27 use files to carry selected memory across fresh iterations. The separation prevents two opposite failures. Without a progress log, the next run repeats investigation and cannot diagnose recurring errors. If every event is promoted to durable instructions, stale attempts and accidental choices pollute future work. Each iteration appends factual execution evidence to progress. Only a discovery that is verified, reusable, and likely to matter beyond the current task is promoted to agents.md. Git remains the authoritative change history; these files explain operational state and learned constraints.
useWhen: Use it for During a database migration loop, iteration 3 discovers that integration tests require a disposable PostgreSQL container and that migration filenames must use UTC timestamps. The failed command and container startup belong in progress.txt. The verified naming rule and canonical test command belong in agents.md. A speculative belief that the ORM has a bug belongs in neither until reproduced.

Use it when prd.json stores atomic tasks and passes flags; progress.txt is short-term iteration memory; agents.md stores longer-lived project patterns. This separates task truth, run notes and durable knowledge.
avoidWhen: Avoid this mechanism when a single deterministic command solves the task with lower coordination cost.

title: Build feedback channels into every Ralph iteration
evidenceNote: Cited PDF pages support the named mechanism. Repository scenarios, exercises, recovery demonstrations, and grading criteria are instructor-authored professional applications.
plainLanguage: A Ralph loop improves only when the environment answers its actions. The prompt supplies intent, but tests, lint, type checks, builds, task state, Git, and curated memory tell the next iteration what actually happened. A feedback channel is useful when its result is captured, attributed to the current change, and converted into an explicit next-state decision. Merely running a command is not feedback if its output disappears or is ignored.
mentalModel: Treat build feedback channels into every ralph iteration as a repository protocol: Tests, lint, builds, task state, git history, and memory become feedback channels. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: The improved loop prevents verifier shopping and missing-output optimism. A predeclared evidence ladder makes each transition reproducible and lets later iterations distinguish product failure, tooling failure, scope failure, and stale state.
mechanism: Pages 27–30 describe an iteration as a closed evidence loop. Task state selects work; focused checks provide fast local evidence; the global suite detects integration damage; Git reveals scope; progress records the trace; durable knowledge prevents repeated mistakes. These channels have different strength and cost. Run inexpensive focused checks early, then the full contract before marking the task passed. The next iteration should receive a concise failure summary and artifact paths, not an unbounded terminal transcript.

The task remains active. The iteration records both failures, removes the unrelated file, repairs the race, and only then advances task state.

title: Earn progression from supervised to unattended Ralph loops
evidenceNote: Cited PDF pages support the named mechanism. Repository scenarios, exercises, recovery demonstrations, and grading criteria are instructor-authored professional applications.
plainLanguage: Ralph autonomy is a promotion ladder, not a switch. Level 1 is one supervised iteration: a person watches selection, edits, verification, state update, and exit. Level 2 is an attended multi-iteration loop: the controller repeats bounded work while a person remains available and reviews checkpoints. Level 3 is unattended execution: the operator may leave, so isolation, budgets, observability, deterministic checks, and emergency stop must carry the safety burden. Success at a lower level is evidence required for promotion, not a guarantee.
mentalModel: Treat earn progression from supervised to unattended ralph loops as a repository protocol: Progress autonomy only after success at lower levels; add iteration, cost, time, and error budgets. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: A correct happy path says little about failure behavior. The promotion ladder tests the control system under realistic work and denied paths. Isolation and budgets limit consequences when the model, task state, verifier, dependency, or environment behaves unexpectedly.
mechanism: Pages 30–43 combine technical budgets with three maturity levels. Iteration, elapsed-time, cost, repeated-error, permission, and risk limits are independent; whichever fires first stops execution. Promotion requires representative traces showing correct task selection, bounded diffs, verifier behavior, state integrity, and clean exits. Unattended execution also needs credential minimization, network restrictions, recoverable checkpoints, remote visibility, and a fail-closed controller. The loop should be demoted after verifier drift, task-schema changes, new external authority, or repeated recovery events.
useWhen: Use it for A monorepo team wants an overnight test-repair loop. They first run five supervised single-test fixes. Next they run a 30-minute attended loop capped at four tasks. Only after clean traces do they permit an isolated overnight run with no production credentials, eight iterations, a two-hour limit, a cost ceiling, three-identical-error abort, branch-only writes, and morning review before merge.
Use it when Watch one iteration end-to-end to learn artifact changes, test behavior, failure shape and token cost before automating repetition.
avoidWhen: Avoid this mechanism when a single deterministic command solves the task with lower coordination cost.

plainLanguage: The Ralph article presents four application patterns, each with a different unit of work and success signal. Feature builder completes scoped product stories. Test-until-green adds or repairs tests in small attributable units. Multi-persona review gathers several role-based critiques; it broadens perspectives but is not independent truth because the same model family and context may share blind spots. Proof-of-concept validator reduces uncertainty with disposable experiments rather than production-quality code. Choosing the pattern first prevents one generic loop from mixing delivery, evaluation, and exploration.
mentalModel: Treat choose ralph patterns by the kind of evidence you need as a repository protocol: Teach four patterns separately; multi-persona review is not equivalent to independent external evaluation. The protocol is valid only when its files and verifier outputs agree.
whyItMatters: Mixed roles share mutable state and redefine success while working. Separated patterns preserve attribution: the POC answers feasibility, the builder changes behavior, the tester challenges it, and the reviewer reports risks. Explicit handoffs prevent experimental shortcuts and self-review confidence from masquerading as verification.
mechanism: Pages 43–53 vary the loop contract rather than merely the prompt wording. Feature work advances PRD task state and requires behavior plus regression evidence. Test work advances a coverage or failure target while guarding against implementation-mirroring assertions. Persona review produces findings, evidence, severity, and disposition—not code by default. A POC answers a named feasibility question under a time box and records what was learned, including negative results. Patterns can be sequenced: run POC before committing architecture, build the chosen feature, improve tests, then conduct fresh review. Their artifacts and stop predicates must remain separate.
